title: Eat halal day to day
whyMatters: Food is usually the first part of daily life that changes for a new Muslim. There is no need to panic about it. Learn the clear basics, make better choices as you go, and ask someone when a detail is genuinely unclear.

subSteps: Stay away from pork and alcohol.
Buy halal-certified meat when you can get it.
Seafood, vegetarian meals, eggs, and dairy make the early weeks simpler, though it is still worth a glance at the obvious ingredients.
Write a short list of staples you know are fine.
Look for halal labels from certifiers you recognize locally.
Do not spend hours checking every minor ingredient at the start.

exactActions.text: Plan for meals with other people
subSteps: Give your host one simple line about what you eat, before the meal rather than at the table.
Offer to bring something you can eat.
At a restaurant, order something clearly fine, and ask when you need to.

exactActions.text: Ask locally about the unclear parts
subSteps: Gelatin, enzymes, cross-contamination, and certification standards all vary.
Ask a local imam or a reliable halal authority when the answer comes up in your life often.
Try not to get stuck on rare edge cases.

timeEstimate: One grocery trip to set up the basics

obstacles.problem: My family cooks with pork or alcohol
obstacles.solution: Start with a respectful request and a practical alternative. If food has become a source of conflict at home, ask a local mentor how to handle it without making things worse.
Stick to simpler cuisines or vegetarian and seafood dishes while you work out which local places are halal. Once you have a short list you trust, it stops being a problem.

tinyVersion: At your next meal, skip pork and alcohol and take the clearest halal option in front of you.
unlocksNext: Once food feels manageable, the wider halal and haram basics are much easier to take in.

gentleScripts.title: For a host
gentleScripts.body: Thank you for inviting me. I eat halal now, so I stay away from pork and alcohol. I am happy to bring a dish to make it easier.
